verse_renderings.text: Because of this, my dear friends, continue to obey as you always have. Now that I am away from you, it is even more important that you do so. Keep living out your salvation with deep reverence and awe.
For God is at work in all of you. He gives you both the desire and the power to do what pleases Him.
Do everything without complaining or arguing with one another,
so that no one can find fault with you. As God’s pure and innocent children, you will stand out in a crooked and corrupt generation, shining among them like stars in the dark sky
as your lives display the message that gives life. Then, when Christ returns, I will have reason to rejoice that my hard work wasn’t wasted.
Your faithful service is like a holy sacrifice offered to God. But even if my life is poured out like an offering over your sacrifice, I am full of joy, and I share this joy with all of you.
In the same way, you too should be glad and share your joy with me.

editorial_resolutions.decision: Display is the chosen contextual sense of ἐπέχω.
editorial_resolutions.rationale: The wording connects the life-giving message with the visible communal witness developed in verses 14–15.

editorial_resolutions.decision: My hard work wasn’t wasted dynamically consolidates Paul’s running and labor imagery.
editorial_resolutions.rationale: The running metaphor is not developed further in this paragraph; the chosen wording preserves the point with less reader friction.
